events.title: Cyrus's Decree
events.description: In the first year of Cyrus's reign over Persia, the Lord fulfills his word through Jeremiah. Cyrus issues a decree allowing the Jews to return to Jerusalem to rebuild the Lord's temple. He also urges neighboring peoples to support them with silver, gold, and other gifts.

events.title: The Return under Zerubbabel
events.description: The heads of the families in Judah and Benjamin, along with the priests and Levites, prepare to go up to rebuild the house of the Lord. The neighboring peoples give them generous gifts, and King Cyrus returns the temple vessels that Nebuchadnezzar had taken away. Zerubbabel leads a caravan of over 42,000 returnees, plus servants and singers.

events.title: The Altar Is Rebuilt and the Foundation Is Laid
events.description: The people gather in Jerusalem and first rebuild the altar for burnt offerings, where they bring sacrifices to the Lord even though they fear their neighbors. They celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles and begin gathering materials for the temple. In the second year, the foundation is laid, and the priests and Levites praise the Lord with trumpets and cymbals. The elderly who remembered the first temple weep loudly, while the young shout for joy.

events.title: Opposition and Work Stops
events.description: The enemies of the people offer to help with the construction, but Zerubbabel rejects them. Then they begin to oppose the project by intimidating the people and hiring advisors against them. They also send letters of accusation to the Persian kings. Under Artaxerxes, they send a letter that leads the king to order the work stopped by force.

events.title: The Prophets Haggai and Zechariah Encourage the People
events.description: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah, son of Iddo, begin to prophesy to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in God's name. Inspired by their words, Zerubbabel and Joshua rise up and resume building the house of God, with the prophets standing beside them for support and encouragement.

events.title: The Temple is Completed
events.description: The Jewish elders continue the construction with progress, driven by the prophecies of Haggai and Zechariah. King Darius confirms Cyrus's original decree and orders that the costs be covered from the royal treasury. The temple is completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of Darius's reign. The dedication is celebrated with great joy, including the sacrifice of one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs.

events.title: The Passover Celebration
events.description: The returned exiles celebrate Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month. The priests and Levites have purified themselves and are all clean. They slaughter the Passover lamb for all the returned exiles, for their fellow priests, and for themselves. Even the Israelites who had separated themselves from the unclean peoples of the land eat with them. They celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days with joy, because the Lord had turned the heart of the Assyrian king toward them.

events.title: Ezra Travels to Jerusalem
events.description: Ezra, a scribe well-versed in the Law of Moses, travels up from Babylon with full authority from King Artaxerxes. The king gives him a letter granting silver, gold, and supplies for temple service, as well as exemption from taxes for all temple workers. Ezra gathers leaders and family heads by the Ahava River. He proclaims a fast to pray for a safe journey, since he was ashamed to ask the king for a military escort. After four months, they arrive safely in Jerusalem with the temple gifts intact.

events.title: Ezra Discovers Mixed Marriages
events.description: The leaders come to Ezra and tell him that the people, priests, and Levites have not separated themselves from the neighboring peoples but have taken their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons. The holy people have mixed with the foreign nations. Ezra tears his clothes, pulls hair from his head and beard, and sits stunned until the evening sacrifice. In a moving prayer, he confesses the people's sin and shame before God.

events.title: The People Repent
events.description: While Ezra prays and weeps in front of the house of God, a large crowd of men, women, and children gathers around him, and the people weep bitterly. Shecaniah suggests that they make a covenant with God to send away their foreign wives and children. Ezra makes the leaders swear to this.

events.title: The Divorces Are Carried Out
events.description: The whole assembly gathers in Jerusalem on the twentieth day of the ninth month. They sit in the open square before the house of God, trembling because of this matter and the heavy rain. A commission is appointed to investigate each case individually. Within three months they complete the work, listing the names of all who had taken foreign wives among the priests, Levites, and the people. They send away their wives and bear their guilt.
